html:
The Byzantine capture of Antioch from Arab rule in October 969, after a blockade begun in 968. The city had been in Muslim hands since the 630s, more than 300 years.

Under Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, the Byzantines were on the offensive in the east, having already won back Crete and Cyprus and much of Cilicia. The local power, the Hamdanid emirs of Aleppo, had been weakened by Byzantine campaigns. In 968 Nikephoros raided Syria and left a force to blockade Antioch. In October 969 a small band under Michael Bourtzes climbed the walls at night and took a tower, and the city fell.

Nikephoros was murdered two months later, and his successor John I Tzimiskes kept the city. Antioch stayed Byzantine until the Seljuks took it in 1084, and was the base for Byzantine power in Syria. The crusaders besieged it in 1097 to 1098 on their way to Jerusalem, during the campaign that ended with the fall of Jerusalem.
